title: GEM-FI: Gated Evidential Mixtures with Fisher Modulation
one_liner: This paper makes single-pass evidential uncertainty estimates less overconfident by suppressing evidence when support is weak and by splitting uncertain regions across several evidential heads instead of forcing one head to explain everything.
lead: Evidential deep learning tries to predict both a class label and its uncertainty in one forward pass. Instead of sampling many models or running ensembles, it outputs evidence values that define a Dirichlet distribution (a distribution over possible class-probability lists). The attraction is speed. The weakness is that one evidential head can still become overconfident, especially near distribution shift or class boundaries, and one head cannot easily express several distinct uncertain explanations. This paper addresses both problems. It learns an internal energy score from features, uses that score to gate down evidence when support is low, then extends the model to a small mixture of evidential heads whose routing uses an added stability penalty so the heads do not collapse onto the same behavior.

problem.h2: Single-pass uncertainty is useful only if low support actually lowers confidence
paras: In evidential learning, the network predicts nonnegative evidence for each class. Large total evidence means the model acts certain, while small total evidence means it stays unsure. In practice, a standard evidential network often assigns too much evidence to inputs that are near decision boundaries or outside the training distribution. That creates poor calibration, meaning predicted confidence does not match measured correctness on held-out data.

A second issue appears when uncertainty is multi-modal. An image can be ambiguous for more than one reason. One part of feature space may sit between cat and dog, while another may contain unusual textures never seen in training. A single evidential head must compress all of that into one uncertainty pattern. The paper's answer is to make evidence conditional on support and to let several lightweight evidential heads specialize to different uncertain regions.

callout.html: Standard evidential learning often acts certain merely because a classifier produced a sharp feature response, even when the feature pattern does not have enough training support to justify strong evidence.

panels.title: 1. Standard evidential head sees one answer
panels.caption: A single head can output high evidence even for inputs that sit in weakly supported regions.

panels.title: 2. Feature energy measures support
panels.viz_args: near training data -> low energy | far away -> high energy
panels.caption: The model learns an energy signal from features that tracks how well the input is supported by training examples.

panels.title: 3. Gate suppresses weak evidence
panels.caption: If support is low, the bounded gate scales evidence down before the final Dirichlet counts are formed.

panels.title: 4. Several heads split uncertain regions
panels.caption: A small mixture lets different heads focus on different uncertainty patterns.

panels.title: 5. Fisher regularizer keeps heads distinct
panels.caption: The final penalty term stabilizes routing so one head does not absorb all inputs and collapse the mixture.

steps.text: A backbone network maps the input into a shared feature representation used by all evidential components.
A small module maps features to an energy value that reflects how well the input is supported by training data.
The energy is turned into a bounded gate so that weakly supported inputs receive less evidence, which lowers confidence before the final class probabilities are formed.
A lightweight mixture assigns routing weights to multiple heads, because different uncertain regions can require different evidence patterns.

steps.b: Stabilize routing with a Fisher-informed penalty
steps.text: The added penalty discourages head collapse by penalizing unstable or overly concentrated routing, so the mixture preserves distinct roles.

paras: The paper changes the evidential output layer in three stages. GEM-CORE adds the energy-derived gate on top of one evidential head. GEM-MIX replaces the single head with several evidential heads plus learned routing. GEM-FI adds a Fisher-informed penalty term that stabilizes those routing weights so the mixture remains diverse and useful.
object.object: evidential output layer and uncertainty control

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: support for the current feature pattern
hidden.name: How much the training data actually justifies strong evidence here
paras: Class probability and support are not the same thing. A classifier can place an input on one side of a boundary and still have weak evidence that the region was well covered during training. The hidden quantity the paper tries to estimate is support in feature space, meaning whether nearby training examples exist with consistent labels. When support is low, high evidence should be suppressed.

The energy module serves as that support estimator. Low energy corresponds to features that fit known training regions, while high energy corresponds to features that sit farther away or in poorly modeled areas. Gating evidence by this score fixes a specific failure mode: the classifier can still express which class is most likely, but it cannot express false certainty when the support signal says the feature region is weak.

heat.caption: The gate exists to separate class preference from confidence strength.

reads.html: The network should be able to say two things separately: which class looks best and how much training support exists for saying that with confidence.

The in-model energy estimate acts as a distance-informed support signal. The gate maps that signal into a bounded evidence multiplier, while the mixture heads preserve several distinct uncertainty patterns in one forward pass.

mechanism.h2: Why gating and mixtures solve different parts of the uncertainty problem
paras: The gate addresses overconfidence. In a standard evidential model, the same feature responses that drive class preference also drive evidence magnitude. That coupling is risky because a feature extractor can respond strongly to unusual inputs for the wrong reasons. By learning an energy score and turning it into a separate multiplier on evidence, the model decouples class direction from confidence strength. A head can still prefer class A over class B, but the gate can shrink both evidence values if the feature support is weak.

The mixture addresses underexpressive epistemic uncertainty. Epistemic uncertainty is uncertainty caused by lack of knowledge rather than by overlapping labels in the data. One head has to represent all knowledge gaps with one evidence pattern. Several heads can split the space so that different heads become responsible for different uncertain regions. That gives the model room to express several kinds of uncertainty without resorting to many randomized repeated passes or a full ensemble.

The Fisher-informed penalty matters because mixtures are unstable without it. Routing can collapse so that one head receives almost everything and the remaining heads become unused. The penalty uses local sensitivity information to smooth and stabilize allocations, which keeps several heads active and makes the boundary uncertainty less jagged.

stages.s: Energy module estimates support in feature space
Gate scales evidential output according to support
Routing weights combine several evidential heads
Single-pass prediction whose confidence matches correctness more closely because low-support inputs have their evidence suppressed before the final uncertainty is computed

math.h2: The gating idea in one line
math.words: Evidence from each head is multiplied by a support-dependent gate before forming the Dirichlet parameters.
symbols: raw nonnegative evidence predicted by a head
learned energy score from the shared features

worked.title: Worked example: same class preference, different support
lines: Input A and input B both have raw evidence [8, 2] for a two-class task.
For input A, the energy module says support is strong, so the gate is 0.95.
The final Dirichlet parameters are close to [8.6, 2.9], which preserves strong confidence.
For input B, the energy module says support is weak, so the gate is 0.20.
The final Dirichlet parameters are close to [2.6, 1.4], which still prefers class 1 but with much lower certainty.
That difference is the whole point of the gate: class preference can remain while evidence strength shrinks when support is low.

math.note: The mixture version computes this kind of gated evidence in several heads, then combines the heads with learned routing weights.

charts.title: Standard evidential model
charts.note: One head can classify well yet still overstate its certainty on weakly supported inputs.

charts.title: GEM-FI
charts.note: The gate reduces false evidence when support is low, and the stabilized mixture captures several uncertainty patterns in one pass.

items.html: If the learned energy score fails to track support in feature space, the gate can suppress evidence in the wrong places or leave bad overconfidence untouched.

items.b: Too many heads can overfit routing.
items.html: A larger mixture creates more flexibility, but it also creates more ways for routing to memorize training regions instead of learning broad uncertainty patterns.
If the Fisher-informed penalty is too weak, head collapse remains. If it is too strong, routing becomes rigid and the mixture loses specialization.
The method is most useful when deployment needs single-pass uncertainty, because it recovers much of the calibration and OOD behavior that usually requires multi-pass methods.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Train three classifiers on the same image dataset: a plain evidential baseline, a gated single-head version, and the full GEM-FI mixture. Evaluate all three on in-distribution test data, shifted data, and clear out-of-distribution examples. Plot confidence histograms, reliability curves, and feature-space maps that show where the gate suppresses evidence and which mixture heads activate. The demo should show that the gated versions keep class preference while lowering certainty in weak-support regions, and that the full mixture separates several uncertain regions more cleanly than one head can.
demo.closing: The decisive check is that uncertainty should drop where support is weak, not merely where the classifier already finds the task easy.
